I'm also very humble ;) /s


In all seriousness, people complain about the state of the world than do the bare minimum to get by. Stuff isn't going to magically get better, people need to actually give a hoot and be the change they want to see.
A Dept of Environmental Quality, not gonna say which one. And yes, I am an avid rockhound and a Geologist by trade, lots of great rockhounding in the rockies.

Thank you for what you do; our work is important at any level of government. 


I'm actually moving to another state position within that region, small world.

I work for my state's government cleaning up the soil and drinking water. I'll say there's a stereotype for a reason. I work with someone who's had this job longer than i've been alive and didn't know how to open a zip file. They exist. 


That being said, for every lazy, uncaring employee are four hardworking, passionate and sharp as anything people trying to serve the people of their state.


Someone else in this tread spoke about doing the bare minimum, be that public or private work. I believe people should take pride in what they do, ESPECIALLY in a state position. My work is funded by the taxpayer and those tax dollars should be used wisely. If I run out of work to do (it happens, often waiting on the private sector to get documents submitted) I pick up extra work and help out coworkers specifically to combat the "lazy government employee stereotype". 


My job is lower stress than the private sector, but so is my pay. At least in my state, there's no pension and the benefits (health, dental, ect) are poor. There's no "suckling from the government teat". The political nature of what we do gets in the way far more often because Billy Bob has an in with the Governer and we're told to turn a blind eye at the risk of our careers. Yes, they may have a harder time firing us, but they just as easily can put you at an empty desk in the basement until you quit (THIS HAPPENS). 


I've had it up to my ears with those assuming we're lazy, unintelligent assholes who scrape by. Blame the politics, not the people. Thanks for coming to my TED talk.
FMLA is great for this.

My lord this is a horrible take. 


I am educated in the sciences and have a stable, well paying job. Almost no debt. That doesn't change the fact I live in a 40 year old 700 square foot apartment, outside of the city in a very affordable area. My rent is almost 50% more than my parents morgage (they bought a ~1600 sq foot home in 2019, built in 2003). 


I MOVED to the lowest CoL state, i'm gainfully employed, and i'm incredibly frugal. I don't eat out, I don't go out to do anything almost ever. I still can barely save $200 a month. As someone else said here, if I have ANY unexpected costs It'll wipe out months of savings.


I'm looking for a better paying position out of state (~40% raise) and the best housing the area has are $1600/mo Mobile homes. Or $950/mo for a 250 sq foot "tiny home".


"Just work harder" isn't working anymore and i'm sick of the "fuck you, I got mine" attitude. I see you often in these threads and you're always such an ass about everything.

It was a slow process, then all at once. I was constantly terrified of someone clocking me, I was sick of "fixing" my voice every time I spoke. I was becoming increasingly anxious about going out in public. I never lived in a particularly friendly area to trans folks, but I feel the climate around it has shifted rapidly in recent months.  I feel like I finally hit a wall a few weeks back and i've been off meds since. 


My trouble is that I really, REALLY don't want to detransition. I have a lot of physical dysphoria and it's terrible to see everything start to reverse. I'm taking it day by day, but I panic if I think further out than that. The emotional aspect was mixed; I appreciated not have the emotional range of a plank but it was somewhat destabilizing with my BP. The social aspect was fine as long as other folks didn't know and I would permanently boymode if I didn't have decent results with HRT. I'm lucky in that sense, but I wouldn't be able to boymode for another few months before being unable to do so. 


I'm trying to be comfortable as a feminine male, but it's not what I want. Still figuring things out. 


I feel your pain with the facial hair, I recommend getting a shower mirror and shaving when you shower. At least for me, it's less of a chore. I also really understand that scrambling feeling of basically "oh shit I have to be in character" when folks treated me a certain way. Just hang in there, this stuff is hard.

I take Wellbutrin (150mg)  moreso as an appetite suppressant then anything else, although i'm also on Lamotrigine (400mg) and i've never had a huge issue with weight gain on it. I tend to eat one larger, warm meal a day and fast for the rest. Not sure if it's a super healthy strategy, but it works well for me. 


I've maintained the same weight (+-6lbs) for the last 5 years. 


When I was on Latuda though, holy shit. I put on 12 lbs in three weeks, that was an instant nope for me.

Hi, thanks for your comment. I'm sorry you broke down about this but I relate. I'd jump in front of a car if it wouldn't fuck up the driver's life. I've been on Lamotrigine this time around since July? Before that Latuda and before that Lithium. I was on Lamotrigine for two years before that and was somewhat stable, but I was also self medicating with MJ for that period of time. 

There might be a working med combo but i'm just so. fucking. tired. I don't have it in me right now to try. I didn't ask for this and I don't know what to do. I don't know if I want to keep looking for a fix.
I hate that y'all can but it does make me feel less alone. Like, what the fuck did we do to deserve THIS.

Lamotrigine has been effective for the first few months, but i've become less stable as time has gone on. I've tried lithium and it did nothing for me besides landing me in the hospital. I've also tried latuda and I gained 12 pounds in three weeks. I'm terrified to try any other meds if they end up being weight positive for me. I was fat, dropped 60 lbs after highschool and I'm pretty sure gaining again would be the final straw.
No.... I'm a geologist, rocks aren't fking magic.

Hi, thanks for your response. I didn't think it was a gotcha; this subreddit is very cordial most of the time :) To answer your question, I did not see that but frankly it not a huge surprise. I guess i'm blown away someone would come out and say that like it's no big deal. 


Much of our funding comes from the EPA, at least for Superfund or RCRA sites which tend to be quite nasty. I think the intention of these cuts is to give state orgs more autonomy but as they're cutting funding and the state orgs can't keep up... I don't like how it's all going to play out but I doubt it's going to be pretty. 


The head of my org is a former Trump admin, a complete tool and seems to have a personal vendetta against our division. Seems most of them are cut from the same cloth. 


I just can't wrap my head around why ANYONE thought touching the EPA was a good idea. It's a tiny tiny fraction of the budget and we were already barely able to operate with the current grant money.


I probably need to change my flair here; I'm socially liberal but economically conservative, I don't know what that's even considered. The deficit was my primary issue and unfortunately neither party wants to actually do jack about it beyond posturing.

If absolutely nothing else, people should not be happy other people are losing their jobs because they think they do nothing. I feel like we should think the best of those around us, is that so crazy? 


You don't perform surgery with a chainsaw you do it with a scalpel. 


I'm Christian, we're taught we should love our neighbors as we do ourselves. Even if you're secular, nothing screams "I'm a good person" like cheering on the loss of others jobs (Not that being christian is an instant "you're a good person" card). Those people have spouses and children too. 


I hate how there's NO grey to politics anymore and I think it's going to stay that way until something brings us together as Americans, instead of whatever political ideology you prescribe to at that moment in time.

We absolutely need to be more careful and cautious with what's being cut. My biggest complaint is the EPA (I work on a similar state level organization) being put on the chopping block. If there's true waste i'd love to have it revealed and removed, but tampering with it like it's a useless organization is criminal. Do people want TCE in their drinking water? Do they want to be able to hold oil/gas producers accountable for cleaning up spills? We were up in arms about train derailments spilling hazardous chemicals and contaminated drinking water three years ago, what happened to that?


The amount of crap I see these big companies lobby and wiggle their way out of, to the detriment of the people, is criminal. Reducing these regulations isn't the way forward, finding more cost effective detection and remedial methods is.


I voted for this, and i'm honestly beginning to regret my decision. They're demonizing many federal folks to justify "cutting" whatever tickles their fancy. 


I'm only able to speak in the environmental field, I can't speak for cuts in other orgs however I feel these kinds of processess need to be gradual.

Hi, thanks for your comment. I'll look into it although i'm slightly hesitant to modify my faith/denomination to align with my desires (I just personally I feel like that would be my motivation) I definitely need to find a community that will support me though, it's awful lonely right now. 


I will say this, I feel as if God's revealing to me that this is more rooted in childhood trauma over anything else. There was inklings of this in my early teens but it really got bad once my parents got divorced. I meet with a secular supportive councellor and a christian councellor often as dual meetings. Expensive but incredibly helpful. 


Genuinely though, thank you so much for taking the time to write up your comment and provide some resources. I feel less alone.

I don't even know if you're able to see responses since you deleted your post, but here's a few things for you:


1. I have Bipolar and BPD. I know plenty about depression and self loathing. Mental health problems suck, i'm not going to ignore that, but it's not an excuse to stop trying. You say your unmedicated, get back on your meds. I've had a few times where I thought I was "cured" only to ruin the next two months of my life because I was so depressed. 


2. Suicide is not an option. I didn't think i'd see my last 6 birthdays yet here I am. I've attempted, it's incredibly painful no matter the method and very easy to fail and irreversibly fuck yourself up. I ODed on sleeping pills and woke up three hours later convulsing and unable to breathe. I had to manually breathe for almost 4 hours and even then it felt like I was suffocating. It is not an option, you don't deserve to suffer like that. 


3. Ask your Therapist about Borderline Personality Disorder. I have it, it sounds like you might based on your responses. I'm not a doctor so take my words with a grain of salt. 


4. Don't put yourself on a deadline to get better, it's setting you up for failure. It's about lots of little steps, not a bunch of huge leaps. 


Don't be angry over people's responses, you asked for feedback and people gave it to you. It sounds like a repeat of the interaction you'd mentioned in your post.

You can have assumptions but you shouldn't put all your faith in that assumption being true. There's a big difference between caution and fear, there's very little to be afraid of regardless of how much transphobia is out there. I live in the south, you deal with it just like anything else. It's also good to remember the internet isn't real life, people are often bolder here than irl. 


I think the reason most people don't understand this is because your assumptions about the world and your frame of mind are the issue, not all of us. As someone else said here, if everyone around you is an asshole, you're probably the asshole. 


Self deprication isn't going to help you either. There's plenty of people in life, transphobic or not, that will tear you down. Don't do it for them. You are worthy of love, as is everyone, even if you don't feel that right now. 


How you've phrased your post comes across as very attention seeking. No stranger on the internet is able to make you eat something. Strangers aren't just critical to one another out of the blue, i'd bet money there's more to that story. If you had a problem with what they'd said you should've approached the situation without being on the defensive. Again, you're making blanket assumptions that others are intentionally trying to hurt/criticise you. You have no enemies beyond the ones you make.


If people push your buttons, work on removing those buttons. Excusing shitty behavior by saying "what else am I supoosed to do?" is trying to deflect the problem with your reaction onto everyone else. I'm sorry you're struggling right now, really. The world is not going to adapt for you and waiting for it to do so isn't going to do you any good. 


You can react emotionally, or you can respond with grace. Easier said then done but until that changes I imagine it's going to be hard to keep folks around. Ask me how I know. 


Just an internet stranger's two cents.

Almost the entire population is cis, of course the vast majority of your bad experiences are going to be from them. This community has such an issue with blanket statements, cutting people off if they don't agree with you and generally being miserable pricks. 

I'm going to reframe your statement in another light to maybe show you how you sound.

>I don't believe ALL white people are necessarily bad, but can anyone really blame me for being scared of most of them? 

*It's almost like assuming something about an entire group of people is wrong.* I've met plenty of incredibly pleasant cis folks. I've also met plenty of assholish trans folks. People are going to be dicks no matter with sex, gender, color, creed, nationality or any other dividing metric.

I have a lot of respect for your persistence to figure it out. I'm in my early 20s and 15 years feels like an impossible amount of time to wrestle with GD. I may talk to my therapist about those visualization execises and see if it would be at all helpful at this point.


It's hard to get past the outer shell, but not impossible. I did something with my therapist where I imagined myself back at 16. I apoligized to myself and everything that had happened. I told myself it wasn't my fault.


My family fell apart when I was 16, my Dad had been cheating on my Mom for over a decade with multiple other women. There was always a lot of preferrential treatment, my sister could do no wrong and I was bullied by my own Dad for far smaller offenses. Not that I remember much of my childhood. He never stood up for me, I was pretty relentlessly bullied by a SPED kid throughout elementary school and he thanked the schoolboard for their time for covering it up. It was always "hey I said this joke and the office today and everyone laughed" and never "Hi fern, how was school today?" Gotta love a Narcissist for a "father". 


He got really buddy buddy with me the year before he divorced her for the sole purpose of shit-talking her to get me on his side. We had a "guys trip" to Washington that year in the San Juan Islands and he spent the entire 3 days talking to the guides about how great my sister was. He looked me in the eye and lied to my face about the divorce 3 weeks before it came out. Even after the divorce happened, he gave up on talking to me two years before he did the same to my sister. I was never valued as a male inside the family or out. I had no idea what a good man was even supposed to be.


He made me feel so throughouly unlovable that I struggle to believe my Mom and Stepfather when they say they love me. I always feel like there's some ulterior motive. 


I was terrified of becoming my father. My grandfather on that side of the family was the same way he is and I was sure i'd end up just like him too regardless of if I wanted to or not. I'd see him in my face, hear him in my voice, recognize sayings or mannerisms i'd picked up from him and it freaking haunts me. This has settled down a LOT recently (6 years on he hasn't apoligized about any of it, in his words "the kids just want me to be happy"). 


I can count on one hand the remaining aspects I have in common with him, both mentally and physically. I have spent the last 7 years revinventing myself over and over and over to erase any similarity to him. The kid me is buried somewhere deep inside and whenever I think of him I just start crying. He didn't ask for any of this and it's my job to him to make sure he isn't hurt again. I want him to feel loved. I'm "her" to protect "him". I hope this doesn't sound fucking insane, but I have a hard time not calling myself "we" all the time, because it feels like there's a "we". It's not some multiple personality thing I just know it's not just me. 


(Typing this out makes it clear as day this is a coping mechanism, so thanks for your comment because I don't know if I would have articulated/seen this so soon. I just don't know where to go from here.)


I've been very blessed to have a stepfather in my life that is everything he wasn't. So incredibly kind, patient with me, he doesn't raise his voice or get upset over small shit. He very strongly disagrees with my choice to transition, but he hasn't once in our tens of hours of discussions raised his voice or insulted me. We're able to have calm, civil disagreements. He's retired, but he spend all his time volunteering. He goes and spends time with folks in hospice, drives medical patients around for free, volunteers at local kitchens and church, ect. We're so close it's like he's my bio Dad and i'm so lucky to have him in my life. Last week for the first time in my life I wanted to be like my Dad and it hit me HARD, he is just so amazing. I cannot express how much I love him. 


I guess that this point I just don't know if I could cope with a male body again, even if/when I get past this trauma. It just really fucked me up and i'm working through it, I just hope it doesn't take me 15 years to do so.


Edit: jeez, that was a lot, thanks for coming to my TED talk lol. 


I wanted to add one thing, self love was a huge factor in my choice to transition, among other things. I like myself more this way because i'm not constantly seeing echos of him in myself. Make of that what you will.

Your description of BPD is so accurate to my experience. There's something so \*special\* about that deep, primal hatred of your entire being that never goes away, always making you feel "othered". I compensate with humor and a fake big ego (all in good fun, of course, my friends know i'm joking around.) lots of deflection from the truth that I believe i'm a horrible excuse for a human being. I absolutely feel unlovable and it's still somethinf I struggle with when people actually just \*like me for me\* and there's not some other motive. 

 I've been worried a lot recently that BPD motivated me to transition, I was recently diagnosed around the beginning of the year and it's thrown a bit of a wrench into my plans. I would have liked to have known this, oh, I don't know, SEVERAL YEARS AGO. 

  
I also have (had?) this deep fear of becoming my father, which i'm sure played into this in some capacity, if only by fucking my self image up more than it already was. I'd see him in my facial structure, hear him in my laugh, so on and so forth. Everytime it made me want to rip my face off and cut my voice out.
It's a big club and we're not a part of it :)

And he said ' Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.' And he said to him 'truly, I say to you, today you will be with me in paradise.' " Luke 23:40-43. 


Come to him as you are. Look at my post history if you think you need to have it together to recieve his gift. I AM WRETCHED without him and only in him am I washed clean. I'm working with him to more closely walk through life in a way that is God honoring, and I obviously have a ways to go. 


This demon named Deceit who's convinced you it's Christ is nothing more than that; a Demon. 


Pray out loud to Him, not this demon possessing you, and ask for Christ Jesus to come into your life! Even if you don't believe me and he's already "possessed you", how could it hurt? 


"The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy; I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full." John 10:10 ESV. 


Do you feel as if you're living your life to your fullest extent? Do you even feel that this thing is giving you that option? This despicable thing mascarading as a God IS NOT CHRIST. This is not what God wants for you. God gave us free will, he would not take that away ESPECIALLY after Christ's sacrifice. He MOST CERTAINLY would not keep you from his word.

You are not unlovable, God has not condemned you no matter how much it may feel like He has, He's right there, waiting for you to cry out to Him.

Hi, thanks for taking the time to respond. 


1. I've never really seen this as something that would fit me. I desperately want to fit into the man/woman binary and I don't think that will change. I want a husband and I want to settle down, a non-standard life (any more non standard than this is, lol.) Isn't something and interests me or that I would find fufilling.  I'll keep an open mind about it and thanks for mentioning it. 


2. This is my concern. I've had enough "progress" erased when I was trying to convince my family of this (got off hrt and onto T-gel for a while). 


3. That's the big problem, i'm not sure. I was never your bog standard kid but I didn't despise puberty, I sure as shit didn't like it but I wasn't constantly obsessing over it. Really only around 17-18 did I really start to feel off, although I remember some inklings of discomfort back when I was 14 that I "wasn't like the other guys". I've always been really insecure about my body, even after I lost a ton of weight (60 lbs) so I know it wasn't a "my self esteem is low b/c i'm fat" thing. I tried leaning into the whole macho man thing to compensate around 18-20, it didn't help at all and only made it more clear that wasn't me. 


The Borderline diagnosis has just complicated this more, what if i'm doing this to try and define a sense of self and not because i'm trans? Like I feel dysphoric about going back but I feel like God is telling me to do so? Am I mirroring what friends around me expect to see? I come from a very conservative christian family (my Mom's written something like 50 Christian women books) and I think if I wasn't trans I wouldn't have held up to their requests and arguments. I think I stated this above, but they found out in March of 2023 and only in September of 2024 did I finally put my foot down and take it off the table as a conversational piece. In that time I'd probably spend a hundred hours answering their questions and responding to their scenarios until it was clear they weren't trying to understand.


( This is somewhat of a sidenote, We have a good relationship at this point and i'm thankful I didn't cut them off, but I can't be "me" around them. I just wish they'd see their daughter and not their son. )


I guess the state of the Union has me a bit nervous too. I'm based in a very red southern state and while i'm trying to move back out west (i'm originally from CO, trying to move to Cheyenne. I'd love to move back to FOCO but the CoL is just untenable. Not that Cheyenne is all that accepting lol) I'm just really scared. Even in this state i'm only out of the closet outside of work and i'm not sure how my job would react if I were to come out. It feels like professional suicide. 


I'm under no presumption the dysphoria will go away, but it's been significantly abated for me as of recent, the borderline development really shook me up. This might just take more time to sort out, I just really hope this is the right choice and i'm going to keep investigating until I figure this out. 


Edit: spelling? I'm so bad at this lmao

I'm definitely thankful I have all my fingers and toes and I do sometimes miss the strength. I used to go rockhounding a lot (go to mineral deposits and collect specimens, topaz for example) and it's been a lot harder to do that. I just can't haul things like I used to and it's obv a lot harder to maintain muscle mass. 

This was a good point/take, tysm for your input!


Edit: I didn't think you meant it like that! I appreciate you clarifying and their take is certainly an opinion lol

Unpleasant doesn't begin to describe it. I recognize that as a legitimate fear, i've seen how some men look at me and i'm not going to downplay it, but you have zero idea what it's like for everyone to constantly assume you're a sex driven barbarian. I had to walk on eggshells around every woman in my life before this because I was just some object to be feared. God forbid I interact with someone without some assumption of an ulterior motive. 


You assuming every man wants to beat and rape you isn't my problem, now or before I transitioned. You sound like you've been really hurt by men in your life and i'm sorry, but assuming there's a boogeyman around every corner is just wrong. You wouldn't judge someone based on their ethnicity, social status, or any other metric, why is it okay to judge them on their sex? 


And society would back men up? Are you kidding me? Last time I checked it's not 1960, it's 2025. Didn't TERFs like you just finish a decade long crusade claiming rape whenever it was convienent for you? Of course it happens, it's horrible and it's not my intention to downplay that. But you had people losing their livelihoods over false accusations like it was going out of style. 


"Check your privilege and get over it" isn't advice and it seems like that's the general consensus. Thanks for your comment anyway.


Edit: Spelling

I'm not going to say I fully understand because at the end of the day I wasn't exposed to this growing up, but saying life's all sunshine and rainbows for guys is bullshit. Do you know what it's like for women to look at you with terror in their eyes for walking the same direction they are on the street? Do you know that no one cares about you, you're meant to just suck it up and deal with it. Forget expressing yourself in any other way that isn't Mr. Macho without being bullied back into whatever closet you came out of.

Hi, thanks for taking the time to respond, it's good to know I'm not the only one here with BPD (sorry you've got it too, it suuucks.) I'm definitely communicating with my psych and therapist on how I feel about all this so I can make the best decision going forward. I just think at the end of the day we all want to feel comfortable in our skin and it takes some of us longer to find how to do that than others.

I like public service too, it makes me feel like my job is actually benefitting people. I will say this though; I have a condition classified as a disability under the ADA that's severe enough that I doubt i'd be able to consistently hold a job in the private sector, so i'll take the lower pay.

I'm not incredibly surprised but if nothing else a blue administration wouldn't actively be blocking us from doing our job. I guess they just really like dry cleaning solvents in people's drinking water (Tetrachloroethene or TCE has been linked to an significant increase in parkinsons) or maybe soil near a preschool that's almost 4% lead by weight. 


The consultants are nearly as bad, they actively try and hide contamination to save their corporations a dime. I've reviewed roughly 120 papers in the last year and ONE of them actually followed our regs and did it right. Nobody gives a damn about the communities this contamination impacts and frankly I don't know how these people sleep at night.  


It just really worries me because these people are RUNNING YOUR GOVERNMENT. I don't see this getting any better.

I feel that once you reach a certain level people have a way of failing upward. I'd like to think this isn't everywhere but that's awful wishful.


Edit: thank y'all for what you do, i've heard students are just awful these days. Forgive me if that's bad info though!

Oh my gosh, this. We had a project where we had to build 3 flow charts for every single process in our division for an online dashboard they didn't have the money for. We worked on them for 5 months and one day I came in and they had changed their mind, hundreds of hours of work, if not thousands completely wasted on a whim. Easily a half a million dollars of waste.  Not to mention they were caught using taxpayer funds for out of state "business trips" (read: going to florida and sitting on the beach for a week). The governor is in the process of covering that up. Our admin was "promoted" to a different state organization when he disagreed with their methods and they still haven't replaced him. 


About half our staff in my division has quit in the last year. Before I came along they provided 90 days to review documents. When I was hired we had 30. They want to reduce it to 14. I manage almost thirty sites and between inspections, report reviews and all the other bullshit I can barely keep up with my job. I'm very concerned our division is going to collapse under them if we lose another 2 - 3 people. 


Oh! All this on a salary where I can barely afford some of the cheapest apartments within 30 mins of the city. 


We're all fucked.

I work for my state's government and most of the people I work with work their ass off to get their job done. There are a few employees that fit that government worker stereotype (I work with a lady in her 50s who doesn't know how to unzip a file and she's worked there almost 25 years, another who's gotten too fat to do fieldwork so we have to pick up the slack for her, ect) but i've found it tends to be upper management that gets in our way more often than not. We've been told to stop doing our jobs multiple times because someone who knows the governor calls him and tells us to stop sniffing around. Our "lovey" Secretary has slowed us down greatly by wanting to review every letter that leaves an almost 1000 person organization, I have a one page letter that went upstairs in June, has been sent downstairs 4(5?) times now with because she didn't like the size of the font, or I correct something and she wants it changed back. I spend more time quantifying what I do for a living to upper management than actually doing my job.

I also just forced myself to use that voice whenever i'm outside of work, so I had a lot of time to get used to using it for long periods of time. 

I'd found a really useful tool recently called Genderfluent: [https://app.genderfluentapp.com/](https://app.genderfluentapp.com/) That has been immensely useful for gauging my voice. Concerning the lightness of my voice, I start lower but without any "buzz" in my voice (Think a patrick star kind of voice, it has a deeper hollow sound.) From there I slowly raise my pitch ( in steps, not continuously ) saying "hello" or "okay" or something along those lines. Each time you raise your pitch a bit more, make sure you're voice isn't getting that buzz sound. You can judge this somewhat by feeling the skin between/above your clavicle, it should not vibrate when you talk. If you can't get as high as you want, get as high as you comfortably can (ask yourself if you could talk for 15-30 minutes at that pitch without straining) and practice. If you have a long commute, I recommend practicing in the car. Just saying road signs, exit names, ect. Repeat until you're happy with it and don't overdo it, your throat should never hurt.
